messages:
diti: quick thread 1: UX follow-up on the 'schema lens' prototype in the playground. aim: one-line summary + quick actions for each tool-call in run history. ryan: saw the mock, looks promising. big question: do we collapse schema details by default? i'm worried about vertical space for long chats. marie: default collapsed. show a compact pill with [3 mismatches] badge and an icon. expand to full field list on click or Space when focused. axel: keyboard-first rules: make the pill tabbable, Space toggles expand, Enter opens full inspector panel. also add Shift+Enter to mark snapshot as accepted. access-bot: accessibility suggestion: use aria-expanded on the pill, and when expanded populate an aria-live="polite" region with a concise summary (e.g., "invocation #42 expanded, 2 type mismatches, 1 missing field"). diti: love that. what about copy for the accept action? current mock says "acknowledge mismatch" which felt vague. ryan: prefer explicit: "Accept as expected" or "Mark as intentional". UX goal: reduce accidental accepts. maybe require a short confirmation for the first accept per session. marie: +1 to confirmation. also add hover tooltip: "Accepting will hide this mismatch from default run-history filters" so users know effect. axel: implementation note: runtime should ideally provide diffs to avoid client inconsistencies. include path-anchored deltas e.g. {path: 'items[0].price', expected: 'number', got: 'string'}. fallback to client diff if runtime doesn't supply. diti: can we include a tiny hash for the accepted snapshot so the backend can store the acceptance against a stable signature? helps if payload changes later. ryan: yes, emit 'snapshot_hash' with the runtime delta. acceptance API should record snapshot_hash + user + timestamp. then run-history UI filters on accepted=true for that hash. marie: copy nit: label the badge 'type issues' not 'mismatches' 1: engineers scan faster for 'type'. also show matching enum values inline when available. axel: keyboard map proposal (short): ``` Tab -> focus next invocation pill Shift+Tab -> previous Space -> expand/collapse pill Enter -> open detailed inspector Shift+Enter -> accept snapshot (confirm dialog) F -> filter run history to only failing invocations ``` access-bot: ARIA sample for the pill: ```
2
Invocation expanded: field user.id type mismatch, expected integer, got string.
``` diti: perfect, save that snippet in the PR. also add a screenshot of the hover tooltip text. ryan: metrics ask: track clicks on 'accept' and how often accepted snapshots later reappear due to downstream changes. helps product decide whether accept is being abused. marie: small UX pedant: the inspector header needs a compact breadcrumb: [model] · [toolName] · [call ts]. put it left-aligned for scannability. axel: dev question: should the run-history list expose a toggle 'Hide accepted' default on? my vote: default hide accepted to reduce noise, but expose a quick 'Show accepted' switch. diti: agree default hide accepted. add a small pill in the toolbar that shows counts: 'Failing: 7 Accepted: 12' so teams can see the ratio. access-bot: final accessibility checklist suggestion to include in PR: keyboard flows, aria-expanded/controls, aria-live phrasing, tooltip text accessible via focus, color contrast for badges, and screen-reader copy examples. marie: i'll update the figma and change the copy to 'Type issues' + 'Accept snapshot' wording. posting link in a sec. diti: thanks team 1: please drop any further nitpicks in figma comments. i'll open the implementation ticket and include the aria snippet, keymap, and metrics requirements in the ticket description. ryan: thanks! going to prototype the accept confirmation modal with the suggested copy.
